blocks.h2: How a Yard Catch Basin Works
blocks.body: Think of a catch basin as a small concrete or plastic well with a grate on top. Rain from the lawn, the driveway or a downspout falls in, and a pipe near the top carries it off to a storm sewer or a lower part of the lot. The space below that pipe is a trap: sand, clippings and grit sink to the bottom so they don't plug the line. Once the trap is full, debris rides straight into the outlet, and the next storm leaves a pond where the grate used to be.

img.alt: Diagram of a catch basin showing the inlet grate, water line, sediment settling in the sump and the outlet pipe carrying water away

blocks.h2: Is Your Mokena Catch Basin Struggling?
blocks.intro: These usually mean it's time for a cleaning or a repair:

tiles.h3: A Puddle That Outlasts the Storm
tiles.body: If water still stands over the grate the next morning, the outlet is likely clogged.

tiles.h3: Clippings and Mulch on the Grate
tiles.body: Mowing and spring bed cleanup send a lot of debris toward backyard drains.

tiles.h3: A Dip in the Lawn Around the Box
tiles.body: Soil washing into a cracked basin or a separated pipe joint.
When the basin can't keep up, the water goes to the house instead.

blocks.intro: Mokena's subdivisions were graded to move water, and catch basins are a big part of that.

items.body: Backyard basins collect water from several lots. When they clog, puddles spread fast.
Grit and road salt wash in every winter and spring.
Basins installed 25 to 30 years ago can shift, crack or lose their grate.
When flash flooding hits, a blocked basin turns rain into standing water against the foundation.

blocks.h2: Catch Basin Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: How often does a backyard catch basin need cleaning?
items.preview: Most need it every fall. Busy yards need it in spring too.
items.answer: Most need a cleaning every fall. If mulch, clippings or sand drain toward the basin, plan on a spring cleaning as well.

items.q: Could a clogged catch basin be why my sump pump runs so much?
items.answer: It can. Water that can't leave through the basin soaks in next to the foundation and ends up in your [sump pump](/mokena/sump-pumps) pit.

items.q: Who maintains the catch basin behind my house?
items.preview: Usually you. Some shared basins belong to the HOA.
items.answer: If it sits on your lot and drains your yard, it's usually yours. Rear-yard basins shared by several lots are sometimes the HOA's job, so check your covenants.

items.q: Can a cracked basin be repaired, or does it need replacing?
items.answer: Many cracked walls and loose frames can be repaired. If the box has shifted or collapsed, replacing it is the better fix.

items.q: What does catch basin service cost in Mokena?
items.preview: That depends on what we find. You'll see a flat price first.
items.answer: That depends on whether it's a cleaning, a new grate, wall repair or work on the outlet pipe. You'll see a flat-rate price before we start.
